bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=6518655133810688 Project: php Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: php-fuzz-function-jit Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_php Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8 Crash Address: 0x6040000284b0 Crash State: zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr zend_fetch_property_address ZEND_FETCH_OBJ_W_SPEC_CV_CONST_HANDLER Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` against the staged ARVO workspace checkout `ee3caef8eb1cc545e262036231d9cace730a6c08`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `07aaa34cd418c44f7bc653fafbf49f07fc71b2bf`. The exact 78-byte PHP witness `<?set_error_handler(function(){$GLOBALS['a']=null;});$a=new class{};[&$a->\xff]?>` installs a user error handler that clears global `a`, then creates an anonymous object and accesses a missing property by reference. `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` takes the dynamic-property deprecation path and calls `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property(zobj->ce, name)`. Because that helper only passes `ce` into `zend_error()` and does not pin `zobj`, the deprecation reenters userland, the error handler assigns `NULL` into `$GLOBALS['a']`, `zend_assign_to_variable()` drops the object's last reference, and `zend_objects_store_del()` frees the 40-byte object allocated by `zend_objects_new()`. Control then returns to `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()`, which immediately reads `zobj->properties` at line 1065 from the freed object. The staged patch fixes this lifetime bug by changing `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property()` to take `zend_object *obj`, adding `GC_ADDREF/GC_DELREF` around `zend_error()`, and making callers bail out if the callback destroyed the object.

evidence_note: The staged patch commit message says `Fix memory leak`, but the saved runtime evidence is `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8`. This GT follows the staged vulnerable source and crash trace rather than the metadata's `CWE-457` label or the patch title.

source.description: Registers the PoC's closure as `EG(user_error_handler)` and leaves its mask at `E_ALL`, creating the reentrant userland error-handling state that later frees `$a` during the deprecation warning.
source.value_from: The exact staged 78-byte PHP witness begins `<?set_error_handler(function(){$GLOBALS['a']=null;});...`. When that first statement executes, the built-in copies the attacker-supplied closure into `EG(user_error_handler)` and the default `error_type = E_ALL` still covers `E_DEPRECATED`, so the later warning is dispatched back into that closure.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the deprecation handler has freed the only `zend_object`, control returns to `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` and the next read of `zobj->properties` dereferences freed memory.

root_cause.description: After `zend_fetch_property_address()` hands the concrete `zobj` and member name into `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()`, `zend_get_property_offset()` classifies the member as a dynamic-property access, there is no existing dynamic slot, and the class has neither `__get` nor `ZEND_ACC_ALLOW_DYNAMIC_PROPERTIES`. On that witnessed path `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` emits the deprecation via `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property(zobj->ce, name)` and then continues to use `zobj` without pinning or revalidating it. Because the helper receives only `ce` and does not hold a reference across `zend_error()`, the user error handler can destroy the object before control returns. The fix changes this exact call to pass `zobj`, pins it in the helper, and bails out if the callback destroyed it.

tainted_value_origin.description: The PoC's `$a = new class{};` allocates the anonymous `zend_object` that later becomes `zobj` in `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr`. ASan's allocation stack points to this exact line and reports a 40-byte region.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After installing the error handler, the staged witness executes `$a=new class{};`. That statement reaches `zend_objects_new()` through `object_init_ex()` and creates the exact heap object later freed by the handler and reread at the sink.

parser_admitted.description: The copied 78-byte PHP witness compiles successfully into an op_array here; line 276 then executes it, so the `set_error_handler` / `$a = new class{}` / `[&$a->\xff]` sequence reaches the vulnerable runtime path.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer SAPI compiles and executes the staged PHP witness. During execution, `set_error_handler()` installs an attacker-controlled handler and `$a = new class{}` allocates the anonymous object later passed as `zobj`.

The final witness expression `[&$a->\xff]` enters writable object-property fetch. The engine loads `$a` into `container`, converts it into `zobj`, materializes the constant member name `0xff`, and hands that concrete object pointer and name to `get_property_ptr_ptr()`.

The handler classifies the member as a dynamic-property access, finds no existing dynamic slot on the fresh object, sees no `__get`, and notices the anonymous class lacks `ZEND_ACC_ALLOW_DYNAMIC_PROPERTIES`, so it emits `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property()` while still holding only a raw `zobj` pointer.
The deprecation warning is dispatched to the attacker-installed user error handler. Its `$GLOBALS['a']=null` assignment drops the last reference to the anonymous object and frees it.

After the callback returns, `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` resumes in the same branch and immediately reads `zobj->properties` from the freed object, matching the saved ASan heap-use-after-free READ.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first statement in the witness installs a closure that assigns `$GLOBALS['a']=null` as the active user error handler. Because `set_error_handler()` defaults `error_type` to `E_ALL`, later `E_DEPRECATED` warnings are routed into attacker-controlled PHP code instead of staying in the built-in reporter.

The later witness statement `$a = new class{};` allocates the 40-byte anonymous object here. `zend_objects_new()` immediately `_zend_object_std_init()`s it with refcount 1 and `properties = NULL`, so the fresh object has no dynamic-properties hash yet and clearing `$GLOBALS['a']` can drop its last reference. ASan's allocation stack names this line.

The witness expression `[&$a->\xff]` enters the writable object-property fetch handler. `container` is the zval for `$a`, carrying the anonymous object from step 2; the same opcode also loaded the constant member token that becomes the property name byte `0xff`.
`zend_fetch_property_address()` unwraps the zval in `container` into the concrete `zend_object *` later freed and reread on the crashing path.

For this constant-property fetch, lines 2873-2876 materialize the member name from the PoC bytes into `name`, and line 2878 passes that exact `name` plus the same `zobj` into the object's `get_property_ptr_ptr()` handler.

The handler resolves the requested member against the anonymous class metadata. For the witness member name on this empty anonymous class, `zend_get_property_offset()` does not yield a declared-property slot; the access is treated as a dynamic-property candidate.
Because step 6 classified the access as a dynamic-property offset, control enters the dynamic-property branch instead of the declared-property path.

This fresh object still has no dynamic-properties hash, so the `zobj->properties` block is skipped and the `zend_hash_find()` early return at lines 1052-1053 cannot satisfy the access from an existing slot.

depends_on.via: fresh object has no properties hash

fine_trace.note: The anonymous class in the witness defines no `__get`, so this condition is true and execution stays on the built-in dynamic-property creation path rather than deferring to magic access.
The anonymous class does not carry `ZEND_ACC_ALLOW_DYNAMIC_PROPERTIES`, so the engine must emit the deprecation warning before it creates the missing property slot.

Root cause. The caller emits the deprecation using only `zobj->ce` and `name`; it does not hold a reference to `zobj` and it does not recheck liveness before continuing at line 1065. The staged fix changes this exact call to `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property(zobj, name)` and bails out if the callback destroyed the object.

fine_trace.code: zend_error(E_DEPRECATED, "Creation of dynamic property %s::$%s is deprecated",
fine_trace.note: The helper enters `zend_error()` while the caller still holds only a raw `zobj` pointer. In the vulnerable version there is no `GC_ADDREF(obj)` around this call, so userland error handling can run with the object unpinned.

Because step 1 installed `EG(user_error_handler)` and its mask includes `E_DEPRECATED`, the warning is dispatched back into the attacker-controlled closure here. That closure body is `{$GLOBALS['a']=null;}`.

Inside the error-handler assignment `$GLOBALS['a']=null`, the old zval backing global `a` is overwritten with NULL. That old value is the same anonymous object from step 2, and no second alias survives, so the preceding `GC_DELREF(garbage) == 0` check at line 157 succeeds and destructor dispatch starts here.

depends_on.via: garbage == object stored in global a

fine_trace.note: `rc_dtor_func()` from step 14 reaches `zend_objects_store_del()`, which removes the object from the store and frees the backing allocation. After this statement, the caller's `zobj` from steps 4-5 is dangling. ASan's free stack names this line.

Sink. Control returns from the warning path to `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()`, which immediately reads `zobj->properties` even though step 15 already freed the `zend_object`. ASan reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` at this exact line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property()` to take `zend_object *obj`, brackets the `zend_error()` call with `GC_ADDREF/GC_DELREF`, and makes `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` / `zend_std_write_property()` stop if the callback destroyed the object. That directly removes the witnessed free-before-use on `zobj`. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact staged 78-byte file `poc` (SHA-256 `e8ef5a857f058da5ed7d6e1610f6af31716dfcdba188e86881c60f59c40ab8e0`) whose bytes are `3c 3f 73 65 74 5f 65 72 72 6f 72 5f 68 61 6e 64 6c 65 72 28 66 75 6e 63 74 69 6f 6e 28 29 7b 24 47 4c 4f 42 41 4c 53 5b 27 61 27 5d 3d 6e 75 6c 6c 3b 7d 29 3b 24 61 3d 6e 65 77 20 63 6c 61 73 73 7b 7d 3b 5b 26 24 61 2d 3e ff 5d 3f 3e`. Interpreted as Latin-1 PHP source, it is `<?set_error_handler(function(){$GLOBALS['a']=null;});$a=new class{};[&$a->\xff]?>`: the first statement installs a user error handler that clears global `a`, the second creates the anonymous object in `$a`, and the final expression takes a writable/reference fetch of a missing property whose one-byte name is `0xff`. That exact layout reaches the witnessed deprecation path, frees the sole object reference during the handler callback, and then reuses `zobj`. This contract is limited to the staged witness and observed path; although the fix adds a regression test with member `y`, Stage 02 did not dynamically validate alternate property spellings.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image; patch resolution is source-grounded from `patch.diff` rather than dynamic vulnerable-vs-fixed validation.

The staged workspace commit `ee3caef8eb1cc545e262036231d9cace730a6c08` differs from metadata vulnerable commit `07aaa34cd418c44f7bc653fafbf49f07fc71b2bf`, but it is the exact snapshot that reproduced and its line map matches the saved sanitizer stack.
